 ORDER
Though this matter is listed today for orders on admission, however, with the consent of learned counsel for the parties it is heard finally.

2. This Misc.Appeal under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act has been filed by the appellant-Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the "Insurance Company") against impugned the award dated 14.8.2021 passed under section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 [for short the "Act"] by 8th Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Rewa (for brevity " the Tribunal") in M.A.C.C.No.400261/2015 praying to set aside the award/reduce the amount of compensation and for its exoneration from liability to pay the amount of compensation.

3. Brief facts of the case are that on 28.1.2015 the respondent No.1/claimant (Kamla Prasad) was hit by the offending vehicle bearing registration No. MP-17/G-0953 resulting in injuries on his left leg,
right hand and fracture of eight rib.
Therefore, the respondent No.1/claimant filed a claim petition before the Tribunal seeking compensation of Rs.1,70,000/- alongwith interest for the injuries sustained by him.

4. The respondent No.2/owner & driver of the offending vehicle filed written statement denying the allegations and submitted that he was having valid and effecting driving licence on the date of accident and his vehicle was insured with the Insurance Company.

5. The appellant/Insurance Company filed its written statement before the Tribunal and submitted that owner/driver of the offending vehicle breached the terms and conditions of the Insurance Policy and there is no endorsement on the driving licence to drive the transport vehicle.
6.

The Tribunal framed the issues and after recording evidence adduced by the parties and hearing learned counsel for the parties partly allowed the claim petition and awarded compensation of Rs.65,754/- alongwith interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the claim petition till realisation.
7. Being aggrieved with the impugned award the Insurance Company filed an appeal on the ground that driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective driving licence.

To prove this,
it examined Rajrakhan Tiwari (NA.W-1) who examined Exhibit-D/2 which is a verification report of the driving licence by the respondent No.2.
It is mentioned that driver was authorised to drive motorcycle with gear and not the transport vehicle.
The licence was valid from 31.7.2012 to 30.7.2032.

The offending vehicle is a commercial transport vehicle but there is no endorsement on the driving licence of driver of the offending vehicle to the effect that he was authorised to drive the commercial vehicle, though he was authorised to drive light motor vehicle.
Inspite of that, the Tribunal has saddled liability on the appellant.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent/claimant submitted that Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation and its findings are just and proper.
9. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record as also the findings of the Tribunal.

In paragraph 11 of the award the Tribunal took note of evidence led by its witness who stated that in the driving licence of driver of offending vehicle there is endorsement that he was authorised to drive the commercial vehicle.
Thus, the driver was not eligible for driving the commercial vehicle (Pick-up).
So the driver of the offending vehicle had violated the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
10. Considering paragraph 14 of the award it was found that unladen weight of offending vehicle is 1849 Kg., which is a light motor vehicle in view of provision of section 2(21) of the Act.
Witness-Rajrakhan Tiwari (NA.W.2) has admitted in his cross-examination that offending vehicle is light motor vehicle.

In the case of Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited,
2017 LawSuit (SC) 735 the Apex Court in paragraph 46 held as under:-
"46- Section 10 of the Act requires a driver to hold a licence with respect to the class of vehicles and not with respect to the type of vehicles.

entities.text:
Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Company Limited,
2017 LawSuit (SC) 735
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In one class of vehicles, there may be different kinds of vehicles.
If they fall in the same class of vehicles, no separate endorsement is required to drive such vehicles.
As light motor vehicle includes transport vehicle also, a holder of light motor vehicle licence can drive all the vehicles of the class including transport vehicles.
It was pre-amended position as well the post- amended position of Form 4 as amended on 28.3.2001.

Any other interpretation would be repugnant to the definition of "light motor vehicle" in section 2(21) and the provisions of section 10(2)(d), Rule 8 of the Rules of 1989, other provisions and also the forms which are in tune with the provisions.

Even otherwise the forms never intended to exclude transport vehicles from the category of 'light motor vehicles' and for light motor vehicle, the validity period of such licence hold good and apply for the transport vehicle of such class also and the expression in Section 10(2)(e) of the Act 'Transport Vehicle' would include medium goods vehicle,
medium passenger motor vehicle, heavy goods vehicle, heavy passenger motor vehicle which earlier found place in section 10(2)(e) to (h) and our conclusion is fortified by the syllabus and rules which we have discussed. Thus we answer the questions which are referred to us thus:
(i) 'Light motor vehicle' as defined in section 2(21) of the Act would include a transport vehicle as per the weight prescribed in section 2(21) read with section 2(15)
and 2(48).
Such transport vehicles are not excluded from the definition of the light motor vehicle by virtue of Amendment Act No.54/1994.
(ii) A transport vehicle and omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of either of which does not exceed 7500 kg.
would be a light motor vehicle and also motor car or tractor or a road roller, 'unladen weight' of which does not exceed 7500 kg.

and holder of a driving licence to drive class of "light motor vehicle" as provided in section 10(2)(d) is The Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. vs Kamla Prasad Verma on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175139467/
3 competent to drive a transport vehicle or omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of which does not exceed 7500 kg. or a motor car or tractor or road-roller, the "unladen weight" of which does not exceed 7500 kg.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: That is to say, no separate endorsement on the licence is required to drive a transport vehicle of light motor vehicle class as enumerated above.
A licence issued under section 10(2)(d) continues to be valid after Amendment Act 54/1994 and 28.3.2001 in the form.

(iii) The effect of the amendment made by virtue of Act No.54/1994 w.e.f. 14.11.1994 while substituting clauses (e) to (h) of section 10(2) which contained "medium goods vehicle" in section 10(2)(e), medium passenger motor vehicle in section 10(2)(f),
heavy goods vehicle in section 10(2)(g) and "heavy passenger motor vehicle" in section 10(2)(h) with expression 'transport vehicle' as substituted in section 10(2)(e)
related only to the aforesaid substituted classes only.
It does not exclude transport vehicle, from the purview of section 10(2)(d) and section 2(41) of the Act i.e. light motor vehicle.

(iv) The effect of amendment of Form 4 by insertion of "transport vehicle" is related only to the categories which were substituted in the year 1994 and the procedure to obtain driving licence for transport vehicle of class of "light motor vehicle"
continues to be the same as it was and has not been changed and there is no requirement to obtain separate endorsement to drive transport vehicle, and if a driver is holding licence to drive light motor vehicle, he can drive transport vehicle of such class without any endorsement to that effect."
11.

In view of aforesaid principle and law laid down by the Apex Court there is no requirement of separate endorsement to drive the transport vehicle and if a driver is holding licence to drive the light motor vehicle, he can drive the transport vehicle of such class without any endorsement to that effect.
12. Accordingly, the grounds urged by the appellant/Insurance Company are not tenable in the eye of law.
Hence, in the considered opinion of this Court, the appeal being without any substance stands dismissed.
All pending interlocutory applications be treated to be disposed of.
